newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Six groups eye Brazil railroad selloff - paper.
newsitem.headline: Six groups eye Brazil railroad selloff - paper.

text.p: Six consortia are interested in bidding in the December 13 auction of a concession to run the South Branch of Brazil's federal railway network, Gazeta Mercantil financial daily said.
The government set a base price of 158 million reais for the 4,000-mile (6,500-km) rail system, a key link to other countries in the four-nation Mercosul customs union, Gazeta said.
Due to its strategic position, the railways selloff should be one of the most hotly disputed in the recently begun privatization of Brazil rail network, the paper said.
According to Gazeta, interested groups include:
* Consorcio Malha Sur, led by Argentina's Industria Metalurgica Pescarmona and including Ferrovia Italiana and U.S.-based Railway Development Corp.
* GP Participacoes, made up of Banco Garantia and Railway Tex of the United States.
* MPE with partner Banco Bozano Simonsen.
* Banco Fator and shipping firm Wilson Sons.
* Brazilian Railway, led by Noel Group.
* Libra group, through its Boreal Participacoes subsidiary.
